doe_orthogonal_array — MULTIVAR plan op

• 数据种类:无 → design(仅由参数决定的算子 —— 不接受图像或数据输入)

• 调用: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.doe_orthogonal_array(name='L9', factors=None, columns=None) -> 'dict'(要直接调用实现,import doe; doe.doe_orthogonal_array(name='L9', factors=None, columns=None) -> 'dict';从台账取用则 opsmultivar.get("doe_orthogonal_array"))

• GPU:无(仅 CPU 参考实现)

用法

正交表 L4 / L8 / L9 / L12 / L16 / L18 / L27（照录自公开发表的表）-> design。

> 以下的详细说明为原文 —— 摘要与标题已翻译。

The arrays are copied from published tables (sources and the copy check in OA_SOURCES), not generated: Taguchi's numbering of columns is what shop-floor literature and the linear graphs refer to, and a generated array with another column order would silently assign factors to interaction columns. Published level symbols 1, 2 (, 3) map to coded −1, +1 (, or −1, 0, +1).

factors: int / names / (name, lo, hi[, unit[, scale]]) (default: one factor per column). columns: 1-based column numbers to assign the factors to, in order (default: the first k columns; for L18 column 1 is the two-level one).

The returned alias lists, for every pair of assigned factors, the columns their interaction falls on and the share (see _oa_interaction_share) — if such a column also carries an assigned factor, that main effect is confounded with the interaction. meta['strength2_ok'] re-checks orthogonality on the table actually used, and meta['regular'] says whether interactions land on whole columns.
